message.content:
獅子（屬於貓科，Carnivora）與斑馬（屬於馬科，Perissodactyla）雖然在現代都屬於脊椎動物，但它們的分化已經相當久遠。兩者最後一次共用一個祖先是在「拉魯西亞特里亞」（Laurasiatheria）這個更大類群內部，距今約七千萬至八千萬年前的古近紀早期。

那時候的祖先是一種小型、以昆蟲為食的哺乳動物，體型像今天的鼩鼱或小鼠，生活在北半球的森林邊緣。隨著時間推移，這個祖先分化成了兩條主要分支：一條演化成了後來的食肉目（包括貓科、犬科等），另一條則演化成了奇蹄目（包括馬科、驢科、犀牛科等）。因此，獅子和斑馬的共同祖先可以說是這種早期的拉魯西亞特里亞哺乳動物。

The user asks: "獅子和斑馬的共同祖先是什麼？" which translates to "What is the common ancestor of lions and zebras?" They want the common ancestor. This is a biology question. The answer: The common ancestor would be an early mammal from the order Carnivora? Actually lions are felids (family Felidae) within order Carnivora. Zebras are equids (family Equidae) within order Perissodactyla. So their common ancestor would be a more distant ancestor before the divergence of the two orders. That would be a common ancestor of all placental mammals? Or maybe the last common ancestor of the two orders: the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be a member of the clade Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of the clade Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor would be a member of the group that gave rise to the Laurasiatheria. But the question might be simpler: "What is the common ancestor of lions and zebras?" The answer: The common ancestor is a mammal that lived around 70 million years ago, likely a small, shrew-like animal that eventually diverged into the lineages leading to carnivores and odd-toed ungulates. So we can say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a small, insectivorous mammal that lived during the Paleocene epoch, about 70 million years ago. It belonged to the clade Laurasiatheria.
